author: Rahul kp
title: Forward vs
simple_words: Both fix today the price for buying or selling later. Forward is a private deal; futures is an exchange deal.

definitions.meaning: A customised agreement between two parties, made over the counter, to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date.
A standardised contract traded on an exchange to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date, with daily settlement.

key_points: Both are ==derivatives==: value comes from an underlying asset
Both lock in a price today for delivery or settlement later
Forward has ==counterparty risk==; futures risk is covered by the clearing house
Futures are ==marked to market== daily; forwards are usually settled only at maturity

insight.text: Forward fits your exact need but carries default risk; futures is standard but safer and easy to exit.

memory_trick.explanation: Tailor stitches to your size, no guarantee he delivers (customised, default risk). Mall sells standard sizes with a guarantee (exchange, clearing house).

steps: Look for margin and daily MTM
exam_tip: In comparison questions, write at least 5 points in a table: market, terms, risk, margin, settlement.

doubt.question: Can a forward contract be traded on an exchange?
doubt.answer: No. Forwards are over-the-counter and customised. Exchange trading with standard terms is the feature of futures.

mistakes.wrong: Futures are customised to the buyer's needs
mistakes.right: Futures are !!standardised!! in lot size, expiry and quality; customisation belongs to forwards.

mistakes.wrong: Forward contracts need daily margin and MTM
mistakes.right: Daily margin and mark-to-market are features of futures; forwards usually have none unless agreed.

mistakes.wrong: Both have the same default risk
mistakes.right: Forward has counterparty risk; in futures the clearing house guarantees performance, so default risk is low.

check_notes: Checker 1: Table row 5, Futures column: 'Daily; often closed out early' is a bit loose. Better: 'Daily MTM of gains/losses, with final settlement (cash or delivery) on expiry; most are closed out before expiry.' Daily MTM settles only the price changes, not the whole contract.

Checker 1: Key point 3: 'futures risk is covered by the clearing house' could be read as covering all risk, including price risk. Better: 'futures counterparty (default) risk is taken over by the clearing house, which guarantees performance.'
Checker 1: Definition 2: 'with daily settlement' would be clearer as 'with daily mark-to-market settlement through margins'.
